monument_name: Devkoṭagāũ Kālikā Devala (built between the 14th-15th cent.)
description_en: Devakoṭāgāũ Kālikā Devala (Temple), dating from the 14th-15th centuries, is located on the eastern rim of the village named Devakoṭāgāũ, two kilometres north of Binayak. A few hundred meters to the south of this Temple is the stone fountain, Champatagaon Navako Dhārā (ACH005).The Temple faces east. Its sanctum is preceded by two columns that support the Temple's pediment (skt.śukanāsāorśukanāsikā). This feature, known asardhamaṇḍapa('half pavilion') in Sanskrit, is unique on this side of the Karnali River. The two columns of the Temple have square bases and octagonal shafts, and the bases are carved on their four sides with images of vases (skt.kalaśa). A cruciform capital crowns the columns, and the right pillar is displaced, with the capital barely resting on it. The threshold bears marks of a door system. The sanctum is currently empty, except a stone block leaning against the back wall. It could have contained a smallśivaliṅga. The ceiling is simply decorated with a single central circular motif. Unless it vanished with time, we do not see the rosette that usually adorns this part of the monument (the surface of the stone seems fragile). There is noāmalakadisc on or around the Temple. Oneāmalakadisc can be found near Champatagaon Navako Dhārā (ACH005). It must have come from this Temple.From the 13th to the 15th centuries, suchśikharastemples were built throughout the Karnali basin (Andolfatto 2019). The rarity of inscriptions onśikharatemples (locally known asdevala) complicates dating of these monuments. The 'half pavilion' (ardhamaṇḍapa) preceding the temple door is a feature found in manyśikharatemples in India, but very rarely in the Karnali basin .Apart from this Temple, only the Ukhadi Devala (JUM0070) in Jumla district has this type of feature (the Ukhadi Devala preserves an inscription recording the date of its construction in ŚS 1408, i. e.,1486 CE) (Sharma 1972, p. 24, Andolfatto 2019, p. 82 and Andolfatto 2022). In contrast to the Ukhadi Devala, the Devakoṭāgāũ Temple lacks anantarāla(skt.) projection on both sides of the doors. These elements suggest that the monument was built between the 14th and 15th centuries. Currently, the Temple is used to worship the goddess Kālikā.When it was surveyed in April 2022, the temple was on the land belonging to Janak Devkota, Brahmin and local resident of Devkotagaon.
monument_assessment: Structural damages, Surface damages, Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)

Paris: Sorbonne Université. Andolfatto, David C. 2022. “Les temples deval de la Karnali (Népal occidental) : réflexions sur leur datation et leur vocation", Arts Asiatiques , Vol. 76, p. 31-46. Sharma, P. R. 1972. Preliminary Study of the Art and Architecture of the Karnali Basin, West Nepal. Paris: CNRS.
